officialTitle: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus placebo plus chemotherapy for previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (KEYNOTE-355): a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase 3 clinical trial
setting: First-line metastatic or locally recurrent inoperable

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between Jan 9, 2017, and June 12, 2018, of 1372 patients screened, 847 were randomly assigned to treatment, with 566 patients in the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy group and 281 patients in the placebo-chemotherapy group.
design.notes: 2:1 randomisation; stratified by on-study chemotherapy (taxane vs gemcitabine-carboplatin), PD-L1 CPS ≥1 vs <1, and prior same-class chemotherapy. Hierarchical testing for PFS: CPS ≥10, then CPS ≥1, then ITT.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding pembrolizumab to first-line chemotherapy improve PFS and OS in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer, and how does benefit depend on PD-L1 CPS?

pico.population: Previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
pico.intervention: Pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks plus chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine-carboplatin)
pico.outcomes: Dual primary: PFS and OS in CPS ≥10, CPS ≥1 and ITT populations. Safety

arms.label: Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Pembrolizumab plus investigator's choice chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel; paclitaxel; or gemcitabine plus carboplatin)
arms.doseSourceQuote: to pembrolizumab (200 mg) every 3 weeks plus chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel; paclitaxel; or gemcitabine plus carboplatin) or placebo plus chemotherapy

arms.label: Placebo + chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Placebo plus investigator's choice chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel; paclitaxel; or gemcitabine plus carboplatin)

publications.title: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy versus placebo plus chemotherapy for previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (KEYNOTE-355): a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase 3 clinical trial.
publications.label: PFS analysis (second interim analysis)

publications.title: Pembrolizumab plus Chemotherapy in Advanced Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
publications.label: Final OS analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Among patients with CPS of 10 or more, median progression-free survival was 9·7 months with pembrolizumab-chemotherapy and 5·6 months with placebo-chemotherapy (hazard ratio [HR] for progression or death, 0·65, 95% CI 0·49-0·86; one-sided p=0·0012 [primary objective met]).
Median progression-free survival was 7·6 and 5·6 months (HR, 0·74, 0·61-0·90; one-sided p=0·0014 [not significant]) among patients with CPS of 1 or more
and 7·5 and 5·6 months (HR, 0·82, 0·69-0·97 [not tested]) among the intention-to-treat population

The median follow-up was 44.1 months. In the CPS-10 subgroup, the median overall survival was 23.0 months in the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy group and 16.1 months in the placebo-chemotherapy group (hazard ratio for death, 0.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.55 to 0.95; two-sided P = 0.0185 [criterion for significance met])
in the CPS-1 subgroup, the median overall survival was 17.6 and 16.0 months in the two groups, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.72 to 1.04; two-sided P = 0.1125 [not significant])
and in the intention-to-treat population, the median overall survival was 17.2 and 15.5 months, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.05 [significance not tested])

safety.description: Treatment-related grade 3, 4, or 5 adverse events (final analysis); deaths in 0.4% vs none
safety.sourceQuote: Adverse events of grade 3, 4, or 5 that were related to the trial regimen occurred in 68.1% of the patients in the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy group and in 66.9% in the placebo-chemotherapy group, including death in 0.4% of the patients in the pembrolizumab-chemotherapy group and in no patients in the placebo-chemotherapy group.

strengths: Double-blind, placebo-controlled randomised phase III design
Prespecified PD-L1 CPS-based hierarchical testing with central PD-L1 assessment
Choice of taxane or gemcitabine-carboplatin partner reflects practice
limitations: Benefit confined to CPS ≥10; CPS ≥1 not significant and ITT not formally tested
Multiple chemotherapy backbones complicate partner-specific interpretation

clinicalImplications.text: Supports first-line pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy for metastatic triple-negative breast cancer with PD-L1 CPS ≥10, making PD-L1 CPS testing a prerequisite.

tumourBoardPearl.text: The PD-L1 cutoff matters: OS benefit was significant only at CPS ≥10, not in the CPS ≥1 group.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMID 33278935 (PFS, second interim analysis, data cutoff Dec 11, 2019) and PMID 35857659 (final OS).
